title: Uniqueness of Shannon Capacity-Achieving Priors
abstract: Formalizes uniqueness of the capacity-achieving input distribution for a Markov-kernel channel in three aligned layers: a finite-alphabet theorem (compactness, continuity, and strict concavity of mutual information on Mathlib's weak topology for `ProbabilityMeasure`), a concrete discharged theorem for compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, and a general measure-theoretic packaging that isolates the abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, plus a counterexample showing pairwise-distinct rows do not give an injective prior pushforward (the non-degeneracy required for uniqueness).

informal.ChannelCapacity.exists_unique_capacity_a: For a Markov kernel between finite alphabets (nonempty input) whose rows are linearly independent (`Kernel.RowMatrixFullRank`), a capacity-achieving input prior exists and is unique.

For compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, given injectivity of the prior-pushforward map and upper semicontinuity of mutual information (the latter carried as a field of `Kernel.ContinuousPositiveDensity`, not derived), the capacity-achieving prior is unique.
General measure-theoretic packaging: under abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, the capacity-achieving prior is unique.
